chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ammar Abu Aasim, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'There are four for whom (supplications) would not be Answered – One of them is the one for whom is wealth, so he spoils it, then he is saying, ‘O Lord, Grace me!’ So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is Saying: “Did I not Command you with the moderation?’
ai.seo_question: Who are the four people whose prayers are not answered according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links the rejection of supplication to the specific sin of wastefulness (israf), contrasting it with the Quranic principle of moderation (al-iqtisad). This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis that material stewardship is a prerequisite for spiritual acceptance, where squandering wealth demonstrates a lack of gratitude and understanding of divine command. The divine response highlights a direct causal relationship between ethical financial conduct and the efficacy of du'a.
